title: Writing style for docs, comments, commits, reports

entries.summary: Write docs, comments, commit messages, and reports in ASD-STE100 style: short sentences, active voice, one instruction per sentence, concise.
body: Sources: Williams, *Style*; Gopen & Swan, "The Science of Scientific Writing". They apply on top of ASD-STE100.
Make the main character the subject and its action the verb.
Unpack nominalizations into verbs: "perform validation of" becomes "validate".
Delete expletives ("there is", "it is"), filler ("in order to", "the fact that", "note that"), and hedges that carry no information.
Put old information in the topic position, new information in the stress position.

entries.summary: Write a code comment only for a constraint the code cannot show.
body: A comment asserting measured or cross-engine behavior is a claim: run the measurement before committing the sentence, and state where it was verified (batch 17 task 3: three false comments shipped, one licensing a real defect, and the fix introduced a fourth).

entries.summary: Document every exported symbol with the language's doc-comment convention. Name things so the code reads without comments.
body: A doc comment states what the item is for, its invariants, and what it returns or raises when the signature does not say so. It never restates the signature.
Conventions: TSDoc in TypeScript, JSDoc in JavaScript, rustdoc in Rust, docstrings in Python — the language's standard form.

Self-documenting code first: full words, verbs for functions, `is`/`has` for booleans, no abbreviation a newcomer must decode, one meaning per name. A comment that explains a name means the name is wrong.
Comments inside a body still follow writing-style.code-comments: only for a constraint the code cannot show.

entries.summary: An instruction keyed to one value of an enumerated field names the value it displaces; test the sentence against every other value before shipping.
body: Batch 10 T2 shipped 'set status to DONE_WITH_CONCERNS whenever concerns is non-empty'. The status enum has four values; as written the sentence also captured BLOCKED and NEEDS_CONTEXT reports, which legitimately carry concerns. The fix was three words: 'instead of DONE'.
Before shipping a conditional instruction into a template or skill, enumerate the conditioned field's full value set and read the sentence once per value it must not change.
Root-only entry: the seed ships no template area, so this loads here through area template (template/**) and is not seeded.

After enumerating the conditioned field's values, enumerate each population's hidden environmental state too, and treat a command output the instruction interprets as itself a conditioned field: read the sentence once per output the command can print in each population. Batch 13's residual: an installed copy older than the merged declaration made the drift line read equal, so the equal-sides reassurance misled in exactly the fired-trigger case.

A gate is an instruction too: when a check is added to a tool, the surrounding protocol's own intermediate artifact states are part of the conditioned state space. Batch 14 T1's hardened validate rejected the retrieval protocol's own write-then-fill draft (terminal status, self_audit null); the fix migrated the flow to audit, fill, validate once, instead of special-casing the draft.

source.ref: batch 10 task 2 review, round 0 Important; HR-036
